questions.question: Define `dead`, `extend`, and `complete`.
questions.expected: `extend(a, i)`: returns the set of partial solutions obtained by extending `a` with one more decision at slot `i`. `dead(b)`: true if partial solution `b` cannot be extended to a valid full solution. `complete(b)`: true if `b` is already a full valid solution.

questions.question: What does branch-and-bound add to backtracking?
questions.expected: A `bound` function on partial solutions and a `bestcost` tracker. Prunes any subtree whose `bound` shows it can't beat `bestcost`.

questions.question: What's a good `bound` function for Knapsack maximization in B&B?
questions.expected: Value-so-far plus the fractional Knapsack upper bound on the remaining items (greedy by value/weight ratio).

questions.question: How does LP relaxation serve as a bound function?
questions.expected: At each search node, solve the LP relaxation of the remaining ILP. Its optimum is a valid bound (upper bound for max, lower for min) on the best full ILP solution extending this partial assignment.

questions.question: When is backtracking better than DP?
questions.expected: When subproblems don't overlap (so DP gains nothing), or the search space is exponential but has good pruning structure (typical for NP-complete problems like SAT, vertex cover).

questions.question: Does backtracking change the worst-case runtime of NP-complete problems?
questions.expected: No — still exponential worst-case. It just performs vastly better on typical instances by pruning.

questions.question: What's the analogue of `dead` for B&B?
questions.expected: The check $bound(b) \geq bestcost$ (for minimization) or $bound(b) \leq bestcost$ (for maximization). When true, prune.

questions.question: For CNF-SAT backtracking, define the roles of `extend`, `dead`, and `complete`. Explain why detecting a false clause under a partial assignment is a valid reason to prune the whole subtree.
